Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the RFP response pack you sent last week. We have a quick set of clarifying questions from our security & procurement teams around data boundaries, activation/egress policies, and proof points for EU-only processing. High level asks: 

- Can you confirm where customer input and model inference ephemeral caches are stored by default (region and service)?
- What are the mechanics and SLAs for region failover if EU capacity is saturated — is there an automated fallback to US/APAC and how is data residency preserved?
- What audit evidence can you provide (configuration snapshots, bucket names, sample audit logs) showing EU-only processing for a sample tenant?
- Any PII minimization strategies — token-level caching retention, KV eviction policy, and encryption key locality?

Could you attach the playbook your team would use to activate EU-only routing and an activation checklist we can include in our attestation? Also point us to any existing SOC2 report or Annex we can share with our auditors.

Hi Laura / Stephanie — following up with the technical details and a pragmatic activation checklist. I focused on behavior that matters for an EU-constrained tenant. Summary first, then the checklist and evidence pointers.

Summary (short):
- Default placement: Customer prompt ingress and model inference occur in the region selected at tenant creation. For EU tenants that is EU1 (Frankfurt) by default. Model shards & worker pods are pinned to EU1 instances; ephemeral KV caches are in-region and backed by EU1-local object storage for short TTLs.
- Fallback behavior: We support policy 'region-prefer' (serve from EU unless capacity exhausted) and 'region-strict' (never egress). With 'region-prefer' the system will failover to a compatible model variant in another region (US-EAST or APAC1) only when capacity policies trigger and only after the tenant consent window (configurable, default 30s) and after masking steps (see egress protections below).
- Egress protections: When cross-region fallback happens we apply three hard controls: (1) PII token filter (redaction) on outgoing payloads, (2) encrypt-in-transit + re-encrypt at destination with customer-specific KMS keys (SSE-KMS) if requested, (3) audit log entry and a tombstone record in EU object store that references the remote processing event.

Playbook (activation + test) — non-destructive run (6 steps):
1) Precondition check — confirm tenant's region tag = EU1 and billing/contract flag for EU-only mode is set.
2) Dry-run routing — flip routing policy to 'region-prefer:dry' (no active failover; records decision path) for 1 hour; collect trace ids.
3) Capacity-trigger simulation — issue synthetic load to emulate 2x normal traffic on EU1 for 15m. Use test-run-2026-09-28.log as baseline.
4) Controlled failover (optional) — set 'region-prefer:active' with tenant consent set to 'auto' and monitor the first 100 requests for PII-redaction hits; abort if >1% failures.
5) Audit artifact collection — export routing traces, KMS key IDs, bucket manifests (sanitized), and the first 24 hours of request headers to shared drive.
6) Rollback — restore original routing policy and purge ephemeral cross-region caches (commands provided below).

Operational details & evidence pointers:
- KV cache retention: default 5 minutes TTL for inference prefix caches; configurable per tenant down to 0s. We can demonstrate the eviction logs (example: test-run-2026-09-28.log) showing key expiration timestamps.
- Storage and logs: EU tenant artifacts (audit logs, billing events, model access indexes) are written to EU1-s3 (bucket arn:aws:s3:::redwood-eu1-audit — we will provide sanitized bucket manifest CSV as evidence). Retention: 90 days by default; configurable to 365 days.
- Key management: by default we use regional CMKs managed by Redwood; customers can supply a BYOK with HSM-backed keys. BYOK keys remain in-custody in EU KMS zones.
- Telemetry & traces: request-level traces include region decision, node-id, and decision-version; we can export a 48-hour sample for auditors (sanitized).

Commands / snippets (ops):
- List ephemeral caches for tenant: redwoodctl cache list --tenant GGF-2026-0731 --region eu1
- Purge cross-region caches: redwoodctl cache purge --tenant GGF-2026-0731 --scope cross-region --confirm
- Flip routing policy (dry): redwoodctl routing set --tenant GGF-2026-0731 --policy region-prefer:dry

Limitations & caveats:
- Cold-start inference (loading large models) may temporarily require control-plane interactions outside EU for container image pulls. Images are mirrored to EU registries; control-plane telemetry for image status may transit to US control plane for orchestration metadata only (no customer data).
- For guaranteed EU-only processing we recommend 'region-strict' policy; note that this reduces available burst capacity and can increase request tail latency during sustained spikes. We will provide latency delta estimates during the dry run.

Evidence bundle we'll provide (sanitized):
- Sample audit manifest (sanitized) showing EU1 processing: audit-manifest-eu1-sample.csv
- KMS key metadata (partial): kms-meta-eu1.txt
- Eviction/test log: test-run-2026-09-28.log

If useful I can assemble a short packet for auditors with the minimal artifacts above and a one-page attestation of processing locality.

Regards,
